interpretation: Imports, simulates and scores. Observables are log10 (lognormal), so -log_likelihood carries the change-of-variables Jacobian -- 993.0497 of the 1255.8661 restored constant. That convention is NOT a caveat: it is verified against the paper's Eq. 6 scale by three solved slugs whose Jacobian is large -- Perelson (log10, +233.1287) at OG = 5e-07, Blasi (ln, -1102.0028) at -4.3e-07, and Laske (mixed lin/ln, +261.0897) at -1e-06. If Eq. 6 omitted the term, Perelson would miss J* by 233, not by 5e-07; a natural-log Jacobian in place of log10 would offset it by n*log(ln10) = 13.34, which the same result excludes. OG_nominal = -8.42 is therefore a real measurement, not a scale artefact: PyBNF at the PEtab nominalValue point scores 8.42 NLL units BETTER than the reference J*, i.e. 4.4x the solved threshold in the wrong direction. Since J* is the best objective over all Marvin runs, that indicates the reference is NOT converged for this problem (k=30, n=286, log10) -- so J* here is a weak reference rather than a target. Independently confirmed 2026-08-07: recomputing this NLL straight from upstream's own simulatedData + measurementData tables, with no PyBNF in the loop, gives 943.9993 -- matching PyBNF exactly. Schwen uses no pre-equilibration, so it is unaffected by lanl/PyBNF#547. Superseded the earlier caveat, which predated any log10 slug being fitted. Import exercised the #510 t=0-only-experiment fix. No optimizer claim -- no fit has been run.
